title: Dust a UR5e's Robotiq 2F-85 gripper on the arm: wipe its deep palm pad and both fingertip pads with only the cloth
instruction: Wipe the dust off the gripper's palm pad and both fingertip pads, touching them only with the cloth, then put the cloth back on the mat.
context: Robot arms that gather training data run with grippers whose pads collect dust, which costs grip. Robotiq's 2F-85 manual names "its two fingertips and palm pad" as the contact grip points and has the gripper cleaned weekly, daily in dirty conditions: "only clean the gripper with a dry towel". O*NET 17-3024.01, Robotics Technicians, core task: "Perform preventive or corrective maintenance on robotic systems or components."
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table. Universal Robots UR5e arm, powered off with its brakes on, bolted to the table at its 149 mm base: base axis at x 769, y -133. It is jogged to a service pose: shoulder axis 162.5 up; elbow axis at x 653, 572 up; wrist 1 axis at x 589, 185 up; wrist 2 axis vertical through x 589, y 0; wrist 3 axis level at 85 up along y 0, its tool flange facing the arms with its face at x 489. On it: Robotiq coupling GRP-ES-CPL-062 (75 mm across, 16.9 thick) and a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper with AGC-TIP-MLD-KIT-85 fingertips, fingers opened fully (85 between the fingertip pads) and lying level, one finger each side of y 0. Its outline is the maker's opened drawing (152.4 across the fingers, 149.3 from its base face to the fingertips). Palm pad: black rubber, 31 wide x 22 tall (22 is an estimate), face at x 385. Fingertip pads: rubber faces 16.2 tall x 38 long, inner faces at y +42.5 and -42.5, from x 326 to 364 (21 to 59 in front of the palm face). All three pads are dusted evenly with white marking chalk through the 1:1 stencil (fixture/zones-1to1.svg). Service mat: grey anti-static bench mat 305 x 610 x 2, x 65 to 370, y -305 to 305 (it passes under the fingertips). Cloth: a 3M Scotch-Brite 2010 microfibre wipe (320 x 360, about 30 g, an estimate) folded into a 120 x 40 strip about 28 thick (thirds across the 360 side, then in half three times: 24 layers, loosely folded; the thickness is an estimate), lying flat on the mat, its long side front to back, centre at x 180, y 200 in lot A (screenshot) and y -200 in lot B. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos, square-on photos of the three pads before and after through the 1:1 zone stencil (fixture/zones-1to1.svg), and a ruler. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment, a robot finger or gripper touches the palm pad or a fingertip pad (only the cloth may; simulation: over 0.5 N of contact), or the cloth falls off the table. Zones: the left and right halves of the palm pad (12 stencil cells each) and the three thirds of each fingertip pad (6 cells each), 8 in all. A cell is dusty if any chalk shows in it; a palm zone is clean with at most 1 dusty cell, a fingertip zone with none (simulation: a cell is wiped once the cloth has slid 20 mm over it, at 5 mm/s or faster, pressing that pad with at least 0.5 N). Every score needs, for the last 1 s, both hands at least 30 mm from the gripper and from the cloth and the cloth still, and at the end the cloth at least 2 mm from the gripper. 1.0: all 8 zones clean and the cloth lying flat on the mat (lowest corner within 3 mm of the mat, tilted 10 degrees or less, all of it inside the mat's outline). 0.75: all 8 zones clean, the cloth anywhere else. 0.5: 5 to 7 zones clean. 0.25: 2 to 4 zones clean. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. Put the used cloth in a bag and lay a fresh folded cloth (the same wipe folded into the 120 x 40 mm strip: thirds across the 360 mm side, then three halvings) flat at the lot's place, long side front to back. 2. Wipe any chalk left on the three pads off with a separate dry cloth; check with a ruler that the gripper is still at its pose (wrist 3 axis 85 mm up, the flange face at x 489; the arm is off and braked) and its fingers fully open (85 mm between the pads). 3. Replace the strips of masking tape over the two arms' finger pads (they keep chalk off the arms' fingers). 4. Lay the stencil over each pad in turn and brush 0.05 g of white marking chalk (weighed on a 0.01 g scale) through it with a soft brush until every zone window is evenly white; photograph each pad square-on with the stencil's 50 mm scale bar in view. Chalk and the used cloth's cleanness are consumed; nothing else is.
fidelity: True size: the 2F-85 outline from Robotiq's opened drawing, its coupling's, and the UR5e's joint centres from UR's published kinematics; covers, link sections and the palm pad's 22 mm height are estimates, all boxes and cylinders. The fingers are fixed open (the gripper is unpowered). The folded cloth is one rigid 120 x 40 x 28 mm block. Dust is 60 cells; one clears after 20 mm of cloth sliding over it at 5 mm/s or more with 0.5 N or more on that pad: a stated rule, not a powder model.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 0 in each; both trials ran to the 2,400-step limit without refusing; the cloth stayed where it lay and no pad was touched); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (all 8 zones clean, cloth back on the mat, released and still; each trial done at about 1,550 steps)
